newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gay protest prompts military muscle flexing.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gay protest prompts military muscle flexing.

text.p: Brazil's military flexed its muscle to prevent about 30 gay rights activists from staging a protest on Monday in front of a revered military monument in the centre of Rio de Janeiro.

Two busloads of military police and dozens of soldiers armed with tear gas, guns and batons milled around the monument in honour of the Duque de Caxias, the founding father of Brazil's military, as the activists gathered a short distance away.

Eugenio Ibiapinu dos Santos, president of gay rights group June 28, said military code 235, which prohibits members of the military from engaging in sexual acts in areas under military administration, was used as a pretext to expulse the protesters.
"In practice this code is used to punish and discriminate against gays in the military," he said. "This is unconstitutional because the constitution is against discrimination.
"It has been proven that being gay and serving in the military are not incompatible," he added.

The protest by gay rights groups Atoba and June 28 of discrimination of gays in the military was prompted by a recent scandal involving a high ranking officer who was found having sex with another man in a car. The officer has lost his command and is expected to be dismissed from the military.

Raimundo Pereira, vice-president of Atoba, said the groups moved their protest a short distance away from the monument for security reasons. He said they had received a number of threatening phone calls warning them against staging the protest in front of the monument.
The activists were preparing a proposal to be sent to Congress demanding a change to the military code.
